jobs.description_text: Young and research-intensive, Nanyang Technological University, Singapore (NTU Singapore) is ranked among the world’s top universities. NTU’s College of Computing and Data Science (CCDS) is a leading college that is known for its excellent curriculum, outstanding and impactful research, and world-renowned faculty. A hot bed of cutting-edge technology and groundbreaking research, the College aims to groom the next generation of leaders, thinkers, and innovators to thrive in the digital age. Located in the heart of Asia, NTU’s College of Computing and Data Science is an ‘exciting place to learn and grow. We welcome you to join our community of faculty, students and alumni who are shaping the future of AI, Data Science and Computing. Job Description / Research Focus: We are seeking to appoint a Research Fellow to contribute to cellular and wireless network security research, with a focus on semantic-aware vulnerability discovery, cross-schema protocol attacks, and multi-agent analysis frameworks. The role covers UE, RAN, and Core Network attack surfaces across the 5G/6G stack, and will foster collaborations with academic partners and industry (Apple, Qualcomm, MediaTek, Samsung PSIRTs, and the GSMA CVD program). Key Responsibilities: Conduct research on semantic-aware vulnerability discovery for 5G/6G cellular protocols and baseband firmware. Design and implement multi-agent LLM frameworks for cellular protocol security analysis. Investigate cross-schema protocol attacks and spec-implementation gap analysis spanning UE, RAN, and Core Network. Prepare and (co-)author research papers in premier venues (USENIX Security, IEEE S&P, NDSS, ACM CCS). Contribute to grant proposals and mentor Ph.D. students and interns. Job Requirements Ph.D. in Computer Science, Cyber Security, Electrical / Electronic Engineering, or a related discipline. Research experience in cellular protocol security, baseband / firmware security, or wireless network security. Experience with protocol reverse engineering, semantic-aware fuzzing, or LLM-based program analysis. Working knowledge of 3GPP specifications and cellular protocol stacks. Publication record in top-tier security venues. Experience with coordinated vulnerability disclosure and industry engagement. We regret that only shortlisted candidates will be notified. Hiring Institution: NTU

jobs.description_text: The National Institute of Education invites applications for one Research Fellow position on a 30-month contract with the Office for Research (OfR) . Project Title: Centre for Special Educational Needs and Disabilities Futures (C-SEND Futures) Project Introduction: Singapore is entering a new phase in the provision of services to persons with special educational needs and disabilities (SEND). Demographic changes and rapid technological developments further intensify both opportunities and challenges within the sector. Artificial intelligence (AI), assistive technologies, robotics, learning analytics, and digital interventions are transforming possibilities for communication, assessment, participation, and personalised support. These developments offer tremendous promise, but also require careful evaluation, ethical stewardship, and translational capability to ensure that innovation meaningfully improves the lives of persons with SEND and their families. The Centre for Special Educational Needs and Disabilities Futures (C-SEND Futures) is being established at NIE as an interdisciplinary platform for translational research, innovation, foresight and capability-building in Singapore and the wider region. It seeks to advance meaningful participation, agency and flourishing among persons with special educational needs and disabilities (SEND) across the lifespan. The Centre brings together researchers, educators, clinicians, policymakers, families, industry and community partners. Its four priorities are interdisciplinary partnerships; knowledge mobilisation; translational innovation and experimentation; and sectoral capability and leadership development. The Centre will be guided by four interrelated priorities: 1. Building interdisciplinary communities and partnerships; 2. Strengthening knowledge mobilisation and dissemination; 3. Supporting translational innovation and experimentation; and 4. Building long-term sectoral capability and leadership. Requirements: The candidate should possess: PhD in education, psychology, special education, rehabilitative sciences, or a related discipline; Relevant experience in research, programme coordination, knowledge translation or stakeholder engagement, ideally in SEND, inclusive education, disability or a related field; Familiarity in the field of SEND, preferably in Singapore; Strong research literacy, including the ability to synthesise evidence critically and prepare clear briefs, reports and practitioner-facing resources; Demonstrated project-management, organisational and communication skills, with the ability to coordinate multiple workstreams and deliverables; Ability to build effective working relationships across academia, government, schools, social services, industry and community organisation; Initiative, sound judgement, independence and a collaborative, inclusive approach to working with diverse stakeholders; Familiarity with emerging technologies (including AI and assistive technology), research ethics, and evaluation methods would be advantageous. Responsibilities: The Research Fellow will support the establishment, coordination, implementation, and operational management of C-SEND Futures. Reporting to the co-Leads of the Centre for SEND Futures, the responsibilities will include: Coordinating interdisciplinary activities and partnerships; Supporting dissemination and translational initiatives; Organising the SEND Futures Forum and related activities; Supporting pilot innovation projects; Maintaining the National SEND Observatory and Knowledge Hub and the web platform; Coordinating communications and stakeholder engagement; Supporting research translation and administrative operations of the Centre; and Any other roles assigned by the co-Leads of the Centre. Application Applicants (external and internal) will apply via Workday. We regret that only shortlisted candidates will be notified. Closing Date Closing date for advertisements will be set to 14 calendar days from date of posting. Hiring Institution: NIE

jobs.description_text: The Lee Kong Chian School of Medicine (LKCMedicine) trains doctors who put patients at the centre of their exemplary care. The School, which offers both undergraduate and graduate programmes, is named after local philanthropist Tan Sri Dato Lee Kong Chian. Established in 2010 by Nanyang Technological University, Singapore, in partnership with Imperial College London, LKCMedicine aims to be a model for innovative medical education and a centre for transformative research. The School’s primary clinical partner is the National Healthcare Group, a leader in public healthcare recognised for the quality of its medical expertise, facilities and teaching. The School is transitioning to an NTU medical school ahead of the 2028 successful conclusion of the NTU-Imperial partnership to set up a Joint Medical School. In August 2024, we welcomed our first intake of the NTU MBBS programme, that has been recently enhanced to include themes like precision medicine and Artificial Intelligence (AI) in healthcare, with an expanded scope in the medical humanities. Graduates from the five-year undergraduate medical degree programme will have a strong understanding of the scientific basis of medicine, with an emphasis on technology, data science and the humanities. We are seeking Research Assistant/Associate to join the Nair group, led by Nanyang Assistant Professor Aditya Nair, to study how neural circuits in the brain process states of emotion. The Nair group combines cutting-edge experimental tools with the development of new AI methods to understand and model complex brain data. Key Responsibilities: Collect large-scale neural activity data and carry out an independent research project. Assist in lab management duties, including purchasing, procurement, budgeting and grant management. Prepare and contribute to grant applications and conference presentations. The candidate is also expected to write and draft research publications in top neuroscience journals, in collaboration with other lab members. Attend a weekly lab meeting and journal club and present data and/or papers as necessary. Key Competencies and Requirements: Bachelor’s degree (for Research Assistant) and Master’s degree (for Research Associate) in life science, neuroscience, computational biology, psychology, or relevant fields. We also invite candidates with interdisciplinary backgrounds to apply. Demonstrated experience in stereotaxic surgery and neural recording experiments in murine models is highly advantageous. Experience analyzing large-scale neural datasets, such as imaging, electrophysiology, or behavioral video data, is preferred but not required. Competent in information visualization. A working knowledge of Adobe Illustrator is a strong advantage . Ability to work independently and collaboratively in a multidisciplinary environment. Entry level candidates are welcome to apply. We regret to inform that only shortlisted candidates will be notified. Hiring Institution: LKC

Who We Are

At OKX, we believe that the future will be reshaped by crypto, and ultimately contribute to every individual's freedom.

OKX is a leading crypto exchange, and the developer of OKX Wallet, giving millions access to crypto trading and decentralized crypto applications (dApps). OKX is also a trusted brand by hundreds of large institutions seeking access to crypto markets. We are safe and reliable, backed by our Proof of Reserves.

Across our multiple offices globally, we are united by our core principles: We Before Me, Do the Right Thing, and Get Things Done. These shared values drive our culture, shape our processes, and foster a friendly, rewarding, and diverse environment for every OK-er.

OKX is part of OKG, a group that brings the value of Blockchain to users around the world, through our leading products OKX, OKX Wallet, OKLink and more.

About the Team

We sit on the front lines of OKX's security and compliance mission. Our charter is to build the flexible, scalable, and intelligent AI systems that detect and prevent identity fraud, account takeover, and large-scale organized abuse — in real time and at the scale of a global financial platform. We own the core identity-risk capabilities that decide, millions of times a day, whether an account can be trusted: identity trust signals, behavioral risk modeling, relationship and cluster intelligence, and face, liveness and document verification. We work shoulder-to-shoulder with Product, Risk, Compliance, and Engineering to turn the hardest adversarial problems in crypto into production-grade defenses that protect good users and the open financial system.

About the Role

We are looking for a Senior AI Engineer to design, build, and own key identity-risk and trust models at OKX. You will build models that combine identity verification results, device and geo data, and user behavior into trust and risk signals, and use graph and clustering methods to uncover organized, industrialized fraud. This is an end-to-end, research-to-production role: you will own algorithms in your domain and ship models into real-money, high-risk, large-scale production environments.
You will be a hands-on technical contributor who works closely with Product, Risk, and Compliance, and who helps raise the technical bar of the team. Your domains span:
  • Identity trust & risk modeling — fusing verification scores, device, geo, and behavioral data into identity-quality and trust signals.
  • Cluster & relationship intelligence — graph and clustering methods to identify account farms, mass registration, and coordinated attacks.
  • Behavioral risk modeling — behavioral features and sequence models for account takeover and abnormal-session detection.
  • Biometric & multimodal signals — face embeddings, liveness/anti-spoofing, DeepFake and injection defense, document forgery and AIGC detection, used as inputs to identity trust and the risk layer.
  • AI agents — applying agentic AI to scale investigation, detection, and operational defense.

What You'll Be Doing

  • Build identity trust & risk models: Design and ship coarse-to-fine risk models that fuse face/liveness/document verification scores, device, IP and geo signals, and behavioral data, for high-concurrency real-time decisioning.
  • Uncover organized fraud with graph & clustering: Build entity graphs across accounts, devices, faces, documents and templates, and apply community detection, clustering, and GNN methods to detect fraud rings and large-scale abuse.
  • Develop behavioral features & sequence models: Engineer real-time and offline behavioral features, and build sequence models to detect account takeover, bot/script behavior, and abnormal sessions.
  • Leverage biometric & multimodal signals: Turn biometric features (face embeddings, face quality, liveness and anti-spoofing results) and document-forgery and DeepFake signals into reliable identity-trust inputs for risk decisions, including biometric similarity for cross-account linkage and duplicate-identity detection. Work with the face, liveness, and document teams, or build models yourself.
  • Drive execution & collaboration: Deliver measurable results while managing ambiguity; partner with backend, product, infrastructure, risk, and compliance teams to integrate models into the production decision chain. Own metric definitions, the balance between false positives and missed fraud, pass rate, monitoring, and drift handling.
  • Advance applied R&D: Experiment with graph learning, multimodal fusion, and AI agents; stay current with academic and industry advances and translate them into practical defenses.
  • Raise the technical bar: Contribute to design reviews, share applied-AI best practices, and mentor junior engineers.

What We Look For

  • 5+ years of hands-on experience building risk-control, fraud-detection, or identity-trust models, including significant experience deploying ML systems into production.
  • Graph & clustering expertise: Experience applying graph mining, community detection, clustering, or GNN methods to fraud or abuse detection.
  • Behavioral modeling: Solid experience with behavioral feature engineering and sequence modeling, including real-time feature pipelines.
  • Deep AI/ML expertise: Strong proficiency with PyTorch and/or TensorFlow, and solid experience with production ML systems.
  • Strong technical & coding skills: Strong coding ability (e.g., Python, SQL) and the system-level thinking to design end-to-end solutions with high availability and low latency.
  • Adversarial mindset: Understanding of how fraudsters adapt, and how to evaluate and iterate defenses against evolving attacks.
  • Collaboration: Strong communication skills, with experience working across engineering, product, and risk teams.
  • Education: Bachelor's degree or higher in Computer Science, Electrical Engineering, or a related field.

Preferred Qualifications

  • Experience in identity verification, KYC/KYB, AML, face-payment or payment risk control, or biometric security.
  • Hands-on experience with face recognition, liveness/anti-spoofing, OCR, document parsing, fake-ID detection, or media forensics.
  • Experience with graph databases or graph computing (e.g., Neo4j, GraphX) and real-time graph features.
  • Knowledge of data and AI/ML infrastructure (e.g., Spark, Flink, Kafka, Airflow, Snowflake).
  • Familiarity with MLOps best practices: monitoring, retraining, and continuous improvement of production models.
  • Experience with LLMs and AI agents.
  • Experience working in fast-paced technology companies or security-critical environments.
  • Research publications, patents, or open-source contributions in relevant AI fields.

  • L&D programs and Education subsidy for employees' growth and development
